notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts cash contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county commissioner, sheriff, attorney and other county office candidates who filed with the NADC since 2023. Candidates file with the NADC once they raise or spend more than $5,000, so smaller races are not included. The NADC files nonprofits with businesses, so both are counted as business money. Individuals, candidates' own money, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Nebraska yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
